scope: Independent AI P81 review of 40 selected, unpublished brief repairs at the listed exact file hashes; no content edits, human approval or release.

checks.register: All 40 revised brief.register fields now state a register or tone and name at least a candidate speaker. Thirty-six specify a plausible listener or audience sufficiently for P81; four still use a generic listener placeholder and are listed below.
checks.grammar: The 16 lessons numbered 2397–2458 now describe tailored reusable grammar patterns, inflections, argument slots or usage constraints instead of only sample sentences. The other 24 retain their pre-existing adequate grammar patterns.
checks.contentStability: Compared each JSON lesson with Git HEAD recursively. Every one of the 40 lessons has exactly a +1 contentRevision bump; changed fields are limited to brief.register, brief.grammar where needed, and contentRevision. No assessment prompts, options, answer keys, models, glossary, target patterns or provenance changed.
checks.build: Fresh focused build and --check pass: 40 lessons, 240 questions, 160 audio requests, 0 structural review flags.

findings.evidence: A colleague, interviewer or writer tells “someone else” how a person seemed. “Someone else” is an arbitrary addressee, not a likely listener for the specific impression-sharing context.
findings.repair: Name a plausible recipient, such as a hiring colleague, interviewee or intended reader, while preserving the existing caution that impression may differ from intent.

findings.evidence: A music reviewer, teacher or family member tells “a listener” that a work connects age groups. The listener role is not tied to the review, classroom or family setting.
findings.repair: Give a paired audience, such as reviewer-to-readers, teacher-to-students, or one family member to another.

findings.evidence: A friend, critic or colleague warns “another listener” about unquestioning allegiance. The recipient is generic despite the clear critical register.
findings.repair: Identify a plausible person receiving the warning, such as another fan, a reader, or a fellow team member.

findings.evidence: A teacher, writer or parent tells “a listener” to use technology as an aid. The recipient remains generic rather than a likely learner, reader or child.
findings.repair: Specify a realistic recipient paired with one of the listed speakers; do not alter the maxim or its assessed examples.

conclusion: The 16 grammar repairs and all 40 revision/content-stability checks pass. Four speaker/listener metadata fields need a more tailored listener before claiming full P81 compliance for this tranche; all material remains unpublished and provisional.
